title: Every input lies in the input set of its own transcript
statement: Let $p$ be a deterministic two-party communication protocol over input types $X$ (Alice) and $Y$ (Bob) with output type $\alpha$, and let $(x, y) \in X \times Y$ be an input pair. Executing $p$ on $(x, y)$ yields a syntactic transcript, and the pair $(x, y)$ itself belongs to the input set of that transcript.
hypotheses_covered: p is a deterministic protocol over X, Y with output type α
replaced:
Let $p$ be a deterministic two-party communication protocol over input types $X$ (Alice)
and $Y$ (Bob) with output type $\alpha$. For every input pair $(x,y) \in X \times Y$,
executing $p$ on $(x,y)$ produces a syntactic transcript $t$, and the pair $(x,y)$
belongs to the input set of that transcript: $(x,y) \in \mathrm{inputSet}(t)$.
